mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 6.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output capacity and earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days during economic slowdowns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.2%) signals imminent monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.2% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS increase > 150,000) signals robust consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases above 150,000 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5%), a decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals impending economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5%), SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad economic slowdown across manufacturing and construction sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
